posts.title: 10 of the Best Swimming Holes Victoria Has to Cool Off in This Summer
posts.description: Victoria’s freshwater swimming holes often fly under the radar, but they’re perfect for days when chlorine and salt aren’t hitting the spot. Ally has scouted some of the best swimming holes Victoria has to splash in, so you can cool off and soak in the sunshine. We acknowledge the Traditional Custodians of the Countries on which these adventures take place who have occupied and cared for these lands and waters for thousands of years. We pay our respects to them and recognise that sovereignty was never ceded. Whether you’re looking for a relaxed swim surrounded by rock pools (check out Ladies Bath Falls in Mount Buffalo National Park) or prefer a picnic day with the fam followed by a splash in shallow water (head to Mackenzies Flat Picnic Area along the Lerderderg River), there’s a swimming hole to suit. posts.title: The Great Victorian Fckery Trail is 45km of the Worst of Victoria’s Nature
posts.description: A new walking trail puts the destruction of Victoria’s nature on the map – literally. Spread over 45km, five routes, and 21 points of interest, the Great Victoria Fckery Trail leads walkers through natural areas in Victoria that are, excuse my French, getting fucked. The five routes can be found in the Yarra and Dandenong Ranges, Mornington Peninsula, Western Grasslands, and Mt Donna Buang and the entire trail is available to follow on AllTrails . Each segment features points of interest that highlight the environmental fckery happening in that area, such as the site of the killing of an endangered Greater glider, the destruction of a 2.8-metre wide Grandmother tree, and the approved location for a rollercoaster-style luge through protected habitat. The points of interest also point out the masses of funding cuts and job losses across Parks Victoria, and the abolition of independent councils once used to provide the government with independent advice on specific natural areas. posts.title: The 9.5km Square Rock Walk Near Canberra Offers Alpine Views & Granite Boulders to Scramble
posts.description: Less than an hour from Canberra, the Square Rock Walk in Namadgi National Park offers stunning alpine views after a gentle ascent through mixed eucalypt forest. It’s not surprising that Elisha believes this 9.5km return walk is one of the best introductions to the Australian Alps. We Are Explorers acknowledges that this adventure is located on the traditional Country of the Ngunnawal people who have occupied and cared for the lands, waters, and their inhabitants for thousands of years. We pay our respects to them as the Traditional Custodians and recognise that sovereignty was never ceded. Quick Overview The Square Rock Walk in Namadgi National Park, just under an hour from Canberra, is one of the best half-day adventures from the nation’s capital. The 9.5km moderate walk is perfect for a range of fitness levels, even achievable for families looking to take their kids on a fun outdoor activity.
